title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 13-15). K is a field of finite type over Q, with E = E_{K̄/K} its arithmetic fundamental (Galois) group. There is an extension 1 → Π_{K̄/K} → E_{K̄/K} → Γ_{K̄/K} → 1. Here Γ is the Galois group of the field of constants, an open subgroup of Γ_Q. Π is the 'geometric' part, Gal(K̄/KQ̄). Grothendieck wants E, and its open subgroups E', to have trivial centralizer in E. The image of the centralizer Z of E' in Γ centralizes an open subgroup of Γ. That image is trivial by the previous page's corollary for Γ_Q, so Z ⊂ Π. One is therefore reduced to showing Centr_Π(Π') = 1 for Π' = E' ∩ Π, which is open in Π.

Corollary. Let π be a profinite group that is a successive extension of free profinite groups. Then the centralizer in π of every open subgroup π' is trivial.

Proof (made explicit). Dévissage: take 1 → N → π → Q → 1 with N free and Q satisfying the property by induction. The image of Z = Centr_π(π') in Q centralizes the open image of π', so it is trivial and Z ⊂ N. Then Z centralizes the open subgroup π' ∩ N of N, so it suffices to treat N free.

Free case. One may assume π' is open normal: replacing π' by its normal core only enlarges the centralizer. π' is free (profinite Nielsen-Schreier for open subgroups). Z ∩ π' lies in the center of π', which is trivial. Hence Z injects into π/π' and is finite. A free profinite group is torsion-free (it has cd ≤ 1), so Z = 1.

Application. Π = Gal(K̄/KQ̄) is such a successive extension. Fibre the function field by transcendence degree. The successive kernels are absolute Galois groups of one-variable function fields over algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0; these are free profinite of infinite rank (Douady, Harbater, Pop). Together with the Γ_Q corollary this gives E with trivially-centralized open subgroups.

Scholie. Since E has trivial center, the connected profinite groupoid Π_{K̄/K} (equivalently the classifying topos B_K) is determined up to equivalence, and indeed up to unique isomorphism, by the associated outer group, i.e. E up to inner automorphisms. Automorphisms of the identity functor of a connected groupoid correspond to the center of the vertex group. The next page extends this to morphisms E_{K'} → E_K with open image: since centralizers of open subgroups are trivial, morphisms of topoi/groupoids are determined up to unique 2-isomorphism by the induced homomorphisms of outer groups. This includes the structural morphism B_K → B_Q, viewed as E_K → E_Q.
errors: The corollary as stated is false if some factor of the dévissage is free profinite of rank 1. Ẑ is abelian, so the centralizer of any open subgroup is all of Ẑ. One must require ranks ≥ 2 (or 0). This is harmless in the application, where the free factors have infinite rank.

The dévissage step is only sketched ('Par dévissage on est ramené au cas d'un groupe libre'). The needed argument, that the image of Z in the quotient is trivial and then Z ⊂ N centralizes the open subgroup π' ∩ N, is correct but not written.

The facts flagged 'à vérifier' are all true and standard: open subgroups of free profinite groups are free, free profinite groups of rank ≥ 2 have trivial center, and free profinite groups are torsion-free. The first two need the rank ≥ 2 caveat.

The claim that Π_{K̄/K} is a successive extension of free profinite groups is implicit. It relies on the freeness of absolute Galois groups of function fields of curves over algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0 (Douady/Harbater/Pop), with infinite rank, which is not stated here.

ideas.what: Groups that are successive extensions of free profinite groups (rank ≥ 2) have trivial centralizers of open subgroups; proof by dévissage, torsion-freeness and centerless free groups
ideas.modern_name: 'Slim' / centrally-trivial profinite groups (Mochizuki's term 'slim'); elastic-type properties of free profinite groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; standard in anabelian geometry (Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg, Mochizuki, Pop); free case in Fried-Jarden
ideas.where_published: Spirit of La Longue Marche (1981) and the letter to Faltings (1983); exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Application to Gal(K̄/KQ̄) for K of finite type over Q, combined with the analogous result for Γ_Q, to get trivial centralizers of open subgroups in the arithmetic fundamental group E_{K̄/K}
ideas.modern_name: Slimness of absolute Galois groups of finitely generated fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Known in anabelian literature (Pop, Mochizuki, NSW ch. XII)

ideas.what: Centerless vertex group implies the connected profinite groupoid / classifying topos is determined up to unique isomorphism by the outer group; trivial centralizers make morphisms with open image determined by outer homomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence between connected groupoids with centerless vertex groups (2-category becomes 1-category) and outer groups; the 'outer Galois action' viewpoint
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, letter to Faltings); standard in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine verifications in the Longue Marche foundations: slimness of free profinite groups and their iterated extensions, and the centerless groupoid / outer group dictionary. All are standard in later anabelian literature. The only flaw is the omitted rank ≥ 2 hypothesis.
transcription_corrections: The insertion '(coté type BK [?])' is more plausibly '(ou le topos B_K)'; the next page speaks of 'homom. de topos B_{K'} → B_K ou de groupoïdes Π_{K'} → Π_K'.
The struck/inserted passage reads approximately 'est connu à équivalence près, défini à iso unique près, quand on connaît le groupe extérieur associé à E_{K̄/K}'.
The two 'à vérifier' margin notes sit beside the lines 'et on admet que le centre d'un groupe profini libre est réduit à 1' and 'élément d'ordre fini ≠ 1'.
The insertion 'On sait que π' est donc libre' is placed above the line 'OPS π' invariant'.
